licensing.open_source: OSI/FSF-approved license or rights-holder public-domain dedication
licensing.source_available: rights holder published source under restrictive or missing license terms
licensing.proprietary: explicit closed-source statement, commercial product, or license limiting distribution to binaries
licensing.unknown: insufficient evidence, including leaked or third-party-preserved code without a license

availability.available: a copy of the source is reachable now
availability.archived_only: source reachable only via an archive such as the Wayback Machine
availability.released_not_located: credible report that source was released, but no copy found
availability.not_located: no copy found; never by itself evidence of closed source

confidence.high: primary statement by the author/publisher or an inspected license
confidence.medium: consistent secondary evidence (wiki category, RWBC flag, unverified license file)
confidence.low: absence of evidence, unverified search summary, or unresolved identity

rules: Freeware binaries without an explicit closed-source statement stay licensing=unknown.
Source of a precursor, successor, or derivative is not attributed to another family.
Third-party mirrors count as available but licensing comes only from the rights holder.
AI search summaries are leads, not evidence, unless the cited primary page confirms them.
